input.quote: c. Limitation on Access. Client will use reasonable commercial efforts consistent with the protection of Client Proprietary Information to restrict access to the Interface to its officers, employees, and agents as may be approved by Client.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds us anywhere in this Agreement, which matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so no redline or comment is proposed. Regex and literal searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "no-hire", "poach", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel", "staff" and "leave the employ" return only § 7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail), the incidental "employees" references in the § 12 indemnities, and § 8(c) (quoted), where "employees" appears solely in an access-restriction covenant and imposes no hiring restraint. Full reads of the two likely locations, § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client, p0050–p0058) and § 10 (Confidentiality, p0061–p0068), confirm the absence. The only restrictive-covenant reference is § 8(d) (p0054), whose cross-reference to the separate "Non-Competition Agreement" is scoped to the limitations on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, not to hiring of personnel. The failed deterministic checks (duration of 12 months or less; general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no non-solicit clause to measure, not defects; the fallback (mutual 12-month non-solicit with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) is unnecessary here. Reviewer note: the separate Non-Competition Agreement sits outside this document, so any hiring restriction living there is not captured by this finding and should be diligenced separately.
